newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle futures end lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle futures end lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower in the wake of Friday's bearish USDA Cattle-On-Feed report, traders said. Trading turned active in closing minutes, with cash-connected buying trimming declines in nearby contracts. Commercial buying was noted throughout much of the session. Although the USDA report was considered bearish, traders said feedlots are current and they doubt feedlots will trade cattle at the $69 per cwt that meat packers bid Monday. The report's September placement figure of 104 percent of a year ago pressured December and February contracts. Some traders relayed that some selling in December was linked to ideas a large share of September's placements could be deliverable against that contract. But other analysts said weight statistics in the USDA report do not support those ideas. The report's weight category showed 65 percent of the cattle placed on feed in September were 700 lbs or heavier versus 64.3 percent in August.
